Q: How to save folds in Vim after changing the foldmethod to diff? A:

IMPORTANT: solution below doesn't work when 'set paste' is active, paste mode disables abbreviations

I don’t use fugitive.vim, but I often use manual folds and vimdiff, so the issue of folds disappearing after vimdiff is quite painful for me.

The usual advice to use :mkview and :loadview doesn’t really solve the problem, so the chances of losing all your folds remain high.

Unfortunately, I couldn’t find any simple solution. My approach is a bit complicated, but it works reliably (tested on Vim 8.0 and 9.1).

Here’s the solution — details below:

function! GetMkviewFoldCommands()
  let tmpfile = tempname()
  execute 'mkview! ' . tmpfile
  let lines = readfile(tmpfile)
  call delete(tmpfile)
  let folds = []
  for line in lines
    if line =~ '^\d\+,\d\+fold$'
      call add(folds, line)
    endif
  endfor
  return folds
endfunction

function! MkviewFilename(filename)
  let filename = a:filename
  if filename[0] != '/'
    let filename = getcwd() . '/' . filename
  endif

  let filename = fnamemodify(filename, ':p:~')

  let escaped = substitute(filename, '=', '==', 'g')
  let escaped = substitute(escaped, '/', '=\+', 'g')
  let escaped = substitute(escaped, '[ \t\n\r"|${}`]', '=%.2x', 'g')

  return escaped . '='
endfunction

function! FoldWrite(filename)
    call writefile(GetMkviewFoldCommands(), &viewdir . '/' . MkviewFilename(a:filename) . '.fold' )
endfunction

autocmd BufWritePost,BufWinLeave,BufLeave * call ConditionalMkview()
function! ConditionalMkview()
  if &foldmethod ==# 'manual'
      let f = bufname('')
      call FoldWrite(f)
  endif
  mkview!
endfunction

function! LoadManualFolds(method)
  if a:method ==# 1
      set foldmethod=manual
  endif
  if &foldmethod ==# 'manual'
      let f = bufname('')
      let files = &viewdir . '/' . MkviewFilename(f) . '.fold'
      if filereadable(files)
        let commands = readfile(files)
        for cmd in commands
          execute cmd
        endfor
      endif
  endif
  if a:method ==# 1
    return 'manual'
  endif
endfunction

au BufWinEnter * call ConditionalLoadview()
cnoreabbrev <expr> manual getcmdline() =~ '^set foldmethod=manual' ? LoadManualFolds(1) : 'manual'

function! ConditionalLoadview()
   call LoadManualFolds(0)
   loadview
endfunction

Why the simple approach doesn’t work smoothly:

au BufWinLeave * mkview
au BufWinEnter * loadview

Suppose you’re editing a file FILE.txt with set foldmethod=manual. You run :wq, and everything seems fine — the fold information is saved to ~/.vim/view/~=+FILE.txt= (the VIMVIEW file).

Then you run vimdiff FILE.txt FILE.txt.old, and Vim automatically changes the fold method to diff. When you quit vimdiff, mkview rewrites the VIMVIEW file, but this time it contains no manual folds, so your old folds are lost forever. (For some reason, when the fold method changes, Vim deletes all folding data for the previous method.)

To prevent that, we need a way to save manual folds separately — so that when foldmethod != manual, mkview can’t overwrite them.

My solution saves manual fold data in a separate file VIMVIEW.fold and restores it when switching back to foldmethod=manual.

Implementation details:

There’s no direct way to extract current fold information (foldclosed(), foldclosedend(), and foldlevel() aren’t enough). The only reliable approach I found is saving the current state with mkview to a temporary file and then grepping the fold commands from it — this is done by GetMkviewFoldCommands().

For storing the fold data, I create a file called VIMVIEW.fold in the viewdir directory. Since VIMVIEW’s naming is a bit special and Vim doesn’t provide a function to replicate it, I wrote MkviewFilename()` for this purpose.

FoldWrite() is simple — it just writes the folding information into VIMVIEW.fold.

Finally, ConditionalMkview() always runs mkview, but saves fold data only when &foldmethod ==# 'manual'.

Loading the folds:

Suppose you open Vim after using vimdiff loadview restores foldmethod=diff, so there’s no manual fold data anymore. When you later switch to set foldmethod=manual, you’d want to automatically reload your old folds — but Vim doesn’t provide an event hook for “foldmethod changed.”

To work around this, I use a small hack with cnoreabbrev. Every time Vim sees the word manual in command mode, it checks if it’s part of set foldmethod=manual if yes, it runs LoadManualFolds(1) to restore data from VIMVIEW.fold.

It’s possible to create a custom command to load VIMVIEW.fold, but then if you accidentally run set foldmethod=manual after using a different foldmethod and write the file, you’ll lose your folds again.

I agree this approach isn’t elegant — but it works. If you know a cleaner solution for Vim 8.0+, I’d love to hear it.

Q: insert multiple records for multiple tables in a single query A:

You can use a CTE. With your definitions, this statement inserts three rows into both tables:

WITH cte AS (
   INSERT INTO person (id)
   VALUES (DEFAULT),
          (DEFAULT),
          (DEFAULT)
   RETURNING id
)
INSERT INTO account(person, uid)
SELECT id, 'uid' || id FROM cte;

But you don't have to insert into both tables at the same time. If you define the foreign key as DEFERRABLE

ALTER TABLE account
   DROP CONSTRAINT account_person_fkey,
   ADD FOREIGN KEY (person) REFERENCES person DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED;

you can use multiple statements withing a single transaction. The constraint only has to be satisfied at the end of the transaction.

Q: I want to delete rows from a Named Range that contains several items listed in MyArray. But I get an error if not found A:

You don't need any error handler when using Find, as long as you check whether it returned a Range (a match was made) or Nothing (no match was made):

Sub DELETE_Db_ROWS_THAT_CONTAIN_ITEMS_IN_AN_ARRAY()
    Dim MyArray As Variant, myValue As Variant
    Dim SearchRng As Range, f As Range, i As Long
    
    MyArray = Array("Reinvest", "DBS", "WDL") 'Delete all rows containing these items
    Set SearchRng = ThisWorkbook.Worksheets("Sheet1").Range("Test_Range")
   
    For Each myValue In MyArray   'loop over each value in the array
        i = 0                     'reset "deleted rows" counter
        Do
            Set f = SearchRng.Find(What:=CStr(myValue), LookIn:=xlFormulas, _
                            LookAt:=xlPart, SearchOrder:=xlByRows, _
                            SearchDirection:=xlNext, MatchCase:=False, SearchFormat:=False)
                            
            If Not f Is Nothing Then 'something was found?
                f.EntireRow.Delete 'remove the row
                i = i + 1
            Else
                Exit Do   'no match: done searching for this term
            End If
        Loop
        Debug.Print "Removed " & i & " row(s) for '" & myValue & "'"
    Next myValue    'next search term
End Sub

Your posted use of error handling breaks a few guidelines - see here for a good overview of how to use error handling in VBA:
http://www.cpearson.com/excel/errorhandling.htm

Adding the typical pointer to why (and how) you should should avoid using Select/Activate in your VBA:
How can I avoid using Select in Excel VBA?

Q: Ask about mobile cross application A:

Can you tell us which technical skills you already have? Learning how to make apps covers many disciplines. You want to know about everything you need to do for a Flutter or a React Native app...? That's a lot if you have no matching skills yet.

Starting with your post's tags - do you know any of the topics you listed there?
The internet is full of free blogs, tutorial videos and documentation about any web development topic. Just search the internet for the topics you want to learn. Flutter and React Native have tons of documentation that you can compare to decide first if they fit your needs.

If you just get a list of the "best tutorials" from us then you don't really want to develop the app yourself - it seems you want to skip a step. Try to get all the information you can, make the decision of the technology yourself. Then you dive deeper.

There are AI-based solutions for creating apps now, but you won't learn much from them if the AI writes the code for you. I think it's still important to seek out the information actively if you want to become an app developer.

If you're just asking "Should I use Flutter or React Native for my app?" then you should make a pros / cons list yourself to help decide. Everything has good parts and drawbacks.
